name: structure-coaching
title: Structure signals coach GREEN, and VALIDATE reports them beside the slice score
outcome: GREEN gets structure coaching when it adds a file, VALIDATE reports structure findings beside the slice score, and the main agent runs each slice through the RED, GREEN, and VALIDATE agents.
done_when: A spike transcript shows one real coach message that carries a structure signal from a project-local habit-hooks plugin, or it records why that route failed
shared/structure_signals.py reports a crowded folder, a name-stem cluster, and a generic file name on synthetic folder trees, and it prints habit-hooks findings JSON
A signal fires only for a file that is new on the branch, and the output names each path that the script did not analyse
The coach is silent for a file that habit-hooks does not scan, it shows three structure findings at most, and it does not repeat a finding in one session
A blind pass of the slice loop text spawns implement:red, implement:green, and implement:validate, and one effect that a script reads shows which agent wrote the slice
The attempt file of a slice holds a Structure block from VALIDATE, outside the overall score, and a failed attempt passes the block to the next GREEN attempt
A replay of five slices or more, with the signals on and off, records the growth of the largest folder and the follow-on resolve rate
One real slice runs locally from RED to a VALIDATE score, and the transcript is kept
abort_if: The spike shows that neither a habit-hooks plugin nor a second runner in habit_coach.py can put a folder signal into the coach message
A hand label of the top findings on three repositories gives a precision below 50% for each of the three signals
The replay shows no difference in folder growth between the two conditions, across several runs for each condition
The structure work needs a hard block on a write, which ADR-0025 does not allow for the coach

min_work.derived_from: 2 districts (implement, shared), 3 colliding ADRs (ADR-0025, ADR-0012, ADR-0038), 1 boundary rule (implement allowed_dependencies), 3 signals, 6 epics
min_work.note: Decided in chat on 2026-11-10, in a cloud session with no bd binary. The engineer kept the GREEN filter, accepted the two coach guards, and asked for a later epic for review and maintenance. No program record exists in the tracker yet. The reviewer round and the runtime diagram are pending, so the stage is decided, not approved.

epics.title: The spike, then shared/structure_signals.py with its three signals and its tests.
epics.outcome: The script reports each of the three signals on synthetic folder trees, only for files that are new on the branch.

epics.title: The coach carries the signals to GREEN, with guides, a cap of three findings, no repeat, and silence for a file that habit-hooks does not scan.
epics.outcome: A stub-binary test shows the coach message with a structure signal, and shows no output for a file that is not scanned.

epics.title: The slice loop text makes the main agent spawn the three agents, and one effect that a script reads shows which agent wrote the slice.
epics.outcome: A blind pass spawns all three agents, and the check fails for a slice that the main agent wrote.

epics.title: VALIDATE writes an advisory Structure block, judges contract drift on the diff, and passes the block to GREEN on a failed attempt.
epics.outcome: The attempt file holds a Structure block, and the overall score does not include it.

epics.title: A replay of slice plans with the signals on and off, a hand label of the findings, and the decision on scored criteria.
epics.outcome: The evaluation record holds the folder growth, the follow-on resolve rate, and the precision of each signal.

epics.title: Review mode and maintenance mode report the structure signals and their trend. This epic starts after E1 to E5.
epics.outcome: A review report and a maintenance report each carry the structure signals, with the four trend tags in maintenance.
